note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a IND 8, 9, 14; A06b IND 8, 9, 14; L05 IND 23(a)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Wedlock restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Wedlock restriction), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a wedlock restriction (a child born out of wedlock may not take it from a citizen father), which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Peraturan Pemerintah Nomor 2 Tahun 2007 tentang Tata Cara Memperoleh, Kehilangan, Pembatalan, dan Memperoleh Kembali Kewarganegaraan Republik Indonesia (implementing regulation of UU 12/2006), hosted by the Directorate General of Immigration's Batam office, Pasal 3(2)(c), (i); PP 2/2007, Pasal 31(1)(a). It confirmed the years of residence, renunciation and loss on taking another citizenship. It was silent on birth in the territory, descent and the limit abroad, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same.
